*[Bug 19038] Wrong as.POSIXct(x, tz="UTC") for POSIXlt object x with x$year near .Machine$integer.max*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19038>

--- Comment #12 from Suharto Anggono (<mailto:suharto_anggono@yahoo.com|suharto_anggono@yahoo.com>) ---
Created attachment 3786
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3786&action=edit>
Against R devel r90397, datetime.c: validate_tm: long long for intermediate
calculation

R fixes up out-of range sec, min, ... by itself, in 'validate_tm'. Integer
overflow is possible.

This uses the same idea of using a wider type than 'int' for intermediate
calculation to avoid overflow in 'validate_tm'. This assumes that long long is
wider than int.

This also makes 'mktime0' doesn't call 'validate_tm' at all if
USE_INTERNAL_MKTIME is defined and doesn't always call 'validate_tm' if
USE_INTERNAL_MKTIME is not defined.

x <- .POSIXlt(list(
sec=0,min=0L,hour=0L,mday=1L,mon=24L,
year=.Machine$integer.max,wday=0L,yday=0L,isdst=0L
), "UTC")
unclass(as.Date(x))
r90185 : negative
Changed: NA

x <- .POSIXlt(list(
sec=0,min=0L,hour=0L,mday=c(1L,30L),mon=1L,
year=2147481800L,wday=0L,yday=0L,isdst=0L
), "UTC")  # not leap year
diff(unclass(as.Date(x)))
r90185 : 28
Changed: 29

x <- .POSIXlt(list(
sec=0,min=0L,hour=0L,mday=1L+7L*146097L,
mon=0L,year=70L,wday=0L,yday=0L,isdst=0L
), "UTC") # mday > 1000000
unclass(as.Date(x))
r90185 : NA
Changed: 7*146097

x <- .POSIXlt(list(
sec=0,min=as.integer(10*146097*24*60),
hour=610L*146097L*24L,mday=1L+600L*146097L,
mon=0L,year=70L,wday=0L,yday=0L,isdst=0L
), "UTC")
unclass(as.Date(x))
r90185 : negative
Changed: 1220*146097

x <- .POSIXlt(list(
sec=0,min=0L,hour=24L,mday=32L,mon=0L,year=70L,
wday=0L,yday=0L,isdst=0L
), "UTC")
unclass(as.Date(x))
r90185 : 31
Changed: 32

*[Bug 19139] New: Supporting SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in html2man*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19139>

            Bug ID: 19139
           Summary: Supporting SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in html2man
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: All
                OS: All
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Installation
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:edd@debian.org|edd@debian.org>

Created attachment 3790
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3790&action=edit>
Reflect SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, if found and suitable, as a build date override

As I have been reporting in a series of recent posts to r-devel, I am
revisiting where the build of R (as source package r-base) fails to build
reproducibly in the Debian build I maintain.

For background, reproducible builds (more at <https://reproducible-builds.org/>)
is a by now more than a decade old initiative R has in fact also supported
since 2015. But the (small) patch we applied then does not squash all
difference. 

This can be seen for the report page off my package at

<https://tests.reproducible-builds.org/debian/rb-pkg/unstable/amd64/r-base.html>

where one can see the difference for various builds of R versions across the
different Debian releases. We care most about what is in unstable now where I
started to make some changes. Following a link in the middle of that previous
page, the current 'residual' is visualized / diff'ed at

<https://tests.reproducible-builds.org/debian/rb-pkg/unstable/amd64/diffoscope-results/r-base.html>

where at the end we see that the generated R.1 and Rscript.1 differ as they
reflect the build date (expressed as month and year).  The 'root cause' is that
the copy in tools/help2man.pl is ancient and itself does not have the upstream
change to help2man ... made in 2015.

I tested a simple patch carried over from upstream.  We init a time variable to
current time (reflecting current behaviour of using system time). If the
override environment variable SOURCE_DATA_EPOCH is found, it is used (and TZ is
reset). That worked for me in a simple test build where I on purpose set the
build date (in debian/changelog) to a future date with differen month and year.
This got picked up by the toolchain to my debian/rules, where I exported it for
the R build so that the resulting binary did in fact show the (imposed here for
a test) future build date.

I attach the patch I used for the build. By the Debian convention it is made
against the r-base-4.6.1 directory, I am sure you can adjust. I used it first
in the SVN tree but have since restored that. I can svn'ify it if needed. I
carried the comment over from the upstream source.  That could be amended if an
explicit reference, or change. But as previous patches I submitted here were
generally tweaked before a SVN commit I am leaving this as is for now. Let me
know if you would want me to alter this as I can submit an updated patch.
